correctness.rationale: A fixed short chord costs 1/(2n-1); two disjoint fixed chords cost 1/[(2n-1)(2n-3)], so short-chord factorial moments give the stated variance. For each different-chord LR pair the opener needs a partner strictly to its right beyond the closer, and the closer needs a partner strictly to its left before the opener. The product of these two counts gives the position formula. Conditioning on B_i leaves a uniform matching when its endpoints are removed; the only added different-chord adjacency is the seam, whose expectation is the stated q_i and vanishes at boundary positions. At n=2 the reduced matching has A=0. An independent mixed-moment derivation counts all LR pairs: the forced LR is removed, no neighboring LR is destroyed, and the new seam is subtracted. Summing the seam probabilities over i gives E L_(n-1), so E[SL]=1+[(2n-2)/(2n-1)]E L_(n-1) and Cov(S,L)=(n-1)/(2n-1). For the LR marginal, insertion immediately after the new first opener gains one; inserting after an old opener gains one unless it replaces an old LR. There are n-k gains in all. The first two conditional moments yield the given variance; affine projection then gives the slope, residual and correlation with strictly positive variance for n≥2. The independent rational recheck propagated the full LR distribution and checked the full-LR seam mixed moment through n=44 (independent_recheck.py); the original enumeration script was read, not executed. The result is not an identity for the nonlinear conditional mean or for cyclic matching.

value.rationale: The count of adjacent openers and closers is a natural local matching statistic. Removing its same-chord contribution reverses a nonzero covariance exactly, and the invariant affine slope and explicit seam effect make the result a useful benchmark for joint matching laws. The value is in the mixed identity and local correction, not in rederiving the known two marginal laws or in claiming independence.
